name: ISIC 2018: Skin Lesion Analysis Towards Melanoma Detection
description: The ISIC 2018 dataset is a landmark benchmark challenge for automated skin cancer diagnosis hosted by the International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) and MICCAI 2018. It comprises three specialized tasks: Task 1 for lesion boundary segmentation (2,594 training, 100 validation, 1,000 test dermoscopic images with binary ground-truth masks); Task 2 for dermoscopic attribute detection (2,594 images annotated for pigment network, negative network, streaks, milia-like cysts, and globules); and Task 3 for multi-class disease classification (10,015 training images corresponding to the HAM10000 collection, 193 validation, and 1,512 test images across seven diagnostic categories: melanoma, melanocytic nevus, basal cell carcinoma, actinic keratosis, benign keratosis, dermatofibroma, and vascular lesion). Users should note that Task 3 training data overlaps directly with the canonical HAM10000 dataset, whereas Tasks 1 and 2 provide distinct boundary and attribute annotations.
